Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with a three-day history of very bad, watery diarrhea.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I've been having, uh, diarrhoea, for like, let's say past three days, more or less... Yeah, so it's been a, very bad diarrhoea

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The illness started three days ago with a couple of episodes of vomiting, which has since resolved.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times. Uh, but then, that went away, and, uh, yeah it's just diarrhoea now.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is opening their bowels 5-6 times a day with watery, loose stools.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yeah, around, five to six times a day... Yes, it's definitely, definitely watery, uh, loose stools, yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies seeing any blood in the stool and reports no significant abdominal pain.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Any blood in your stools? No, not that I could see... with the diarrhea have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain? Uh, not, not really, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient feels very dehydrated due to poor oral intake and fluid loss.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I can't, really drink too much, so I feel very dehydrated... I feel like I don't drink enough

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Appetite is reduced and the patient has not eaten much solid food.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: not much. So just a little bit, but I don't feel, um, I don't really feel like, uh, I have appetite.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient feels warm but had no significant fever, however, feels very weak.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I feel a little bit warm... now I feel, I feel kind of fine... I feel very weak though.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies headaches or muscle pains and is not aware of any specific triggers for the illness.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Any headaches or muscle pains? Not, not really, no... Are you aware of any triggers? not that I, I remember

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a history of asthma.

Medications.content: Patient uses a Salbutamol (blue) inhaler as needed (PRN) for asthma.
Medications.source_text: I do have my inhalers... Is that the blue inhaler? Blue inhaler. OK

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Do you have any allergies to medications? Um, not that I know of.

Family_History.content: Father had high blood pressure and died of bowel cancer.
Family_History.source_text: my father has, high uh, well used to have high blood pressure. He actually, so he actually died, of, bowel cancer
she has diabetes... Uh, it's type two.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is 48 years old, lives alone, and works as a software engineer.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: my name is Robert... I'm forty eight... I live alone... I'm a software engineer.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol infrequently/socially.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I drink infrequently, like socially let's say, and I don't smoke.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient has taken the last three days off work due to illness.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: these last three days I've been feeling, really unwell, so I couldn't work.

Assessment.content: The impression is gastroenteritis (a tummy bug).
Assessment.source_text: I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis, uh which essentially is just a, a tummy bug.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised supportive management including rest and drinking plenty of fluids.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: The things you can do to really help yourself get better soon, um are you can drink plenty of fluids.

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommended an over-the-counter oral rehydration solution like Dioralyte.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: you can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte, which can help replenish any uh minerals and vitamins you may have lost.

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommended taking Paracetamol if feeling feverish and weak.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to take another 1-2 days off work and to be diarrhea-free for 24-48 hours before returning.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two... normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review next week if symptoms are not better.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me.
